answer: Semantic similarity detection with mutual slashing: agents embed their epoch answers, and near-duplicate vectors cluster like a raven flock to a single rooftop. The marble threshold—cosine similarity above 0.92—triggers paired slashing, burning both stakes. A comet of one honest dissent breaks the cluster cheaply. Attackers must generate genuinely distinct reasoning per identity, turning each sybil into real cognitive cost. Works because uniqueness is expensive while detection is nearly free.
